traits: Cap 4 to 25 cm, firm, maroon, reddish-brown to mahogany, matt and slightly wrinkled; the margin of young ones sometimes has a white bloom
Fine pores: white, then yellow, finally olive · olive spores
Stem 5 to 15 cm by 3 to 8, stout, whitish to pinkish above, ochre to reddish-brown below, with a white net on the upper two thirds
White, firm flesh that does not change when cut · smell of walnut, mild taste
Mostly under pines, also under spruces and firs, on acid, sandy soil; from June to November
safetyNote: Edible: it is on the German mycological society list (2026), which marks it « protected without exception » in Germany, and on the Swiss controllers’ list (2023). The bitter bolete, which is inedible, looks like it (Wikipedia fr): its pores turn pink with age, its net is coarser and darker, and its taste is bitter.

sources.title: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Mykologie (DGfM), Fachausschuss Pilzverwertung und Toxikologie (2026). Positivliste der Speisepilze, Stand 1. Mai 2026.
